correctness.rationale: The proof reduces arbitrary skew parallelograms to sidewise isometric rectangle arclength sampling and derives exact expected area by cyclic consecutive-pair shoelace counting. Distributional fourth differentiation of the rectangle correlation gives the explicit cubic spline, with direct check of jump terms and boundary data. Elementary Beta integration obtains the stated N-dependent expression, and a finite positive binomial expansion valid for every integer N>=3 proves strict imbalance ordering and sharp endpoints. Exact rational and independent boundary-sampling checks of CHECK.py pass; the infinite statement is justified analytically, not by finite tests.

value.rationale: The expected missing area of boundary-inscribed random polygons is an established nontrivial geometric-probability invariant. The new theorem supplies exact finite-N evaluation, all-N sharp shape ordering and a complete degeneration limit for the full two-parameter side ratio and shear family. The angle-independence gives a structural invariance; the strict rhombus extremality and exponentially small finite corrections cannot be read off from the known general N^-2 asymptotics. The formula is neither a numerical slice nor a routine renaming of an existing identity.
